about.title: Personal Injury Help in Williams, California
about.longDescription: Williams is a small city, but its roads carry a lot of pass-through and local traffic. Rt 20 and I-5 both run through town, and E Street and 8th Street handle much of the day-to-day local traffic. In the most recent full year on record, Williams saw 10 injury collisions, 14 people hurt, and 1 traffic death — public numbers that show real people dealing with real injuries. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, or in any accident around town, sorting out medical bills, insurance calls, and lost work time can feel like a second job on top of recovering. We're here to help injured people in Williams understand their options and guide them through the process. Our team works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover money. Reaching out costs nothing and there's no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: California's Filing Deadline
items.desc: Most injury claims in California must be filed within two years of the incident, and claims against a government agency can require notice in as little as six months. Waiting too long can mean losing the right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Shared Fault Doesn't Block You
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for what happened, you may still be able to recover compensation reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life, unlike some other states.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: We work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover money. There's no hourly billing and no upfront cost to find out where you stand.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing. There's no cost for your free case review. If you move forward and we take your case, we work on contingency, so we only get paid if you recover compensation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after an accident in Williams?
items.answer: In California, most personal injury claims must be filed within two years of the date of the incident. If a government entity is involved, such as a city or county road issue, the notice deadline can be as short as six months, so it's best not to wait.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Williams?
items.answer: Public collision records show higher counts along corridors like Rt 20, I-5, E Street, and 8th Street, with reported crashes tending to peak on Fridays between 4 and 6 p.m. These are simply recorded crash counts, not a judgment about any road being unsafe.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, which means being partly responsible doesn't automatically bar you from recovering money. Your compensation would typically be reduced by your percentage of fault, but you may still have a valid claim worth discussing.

items.question: Does your firm represent me directly?
items.answer: Yes. Our team handles personal injury claims in Williams and throughout Colusa County. We represent you directly and work on contingency — no upfront fees.
